newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close little changed. [CORRECTED 16:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close little changed. [CORRECTED 16:30 GMT]

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Monday (corrects day) in volatile trading spurred by heavy trading in Maof options, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.03 percent, or 0.08 points, to 271.14 on all-share turnover of 124 million shekels against 130 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.03 percent higher at 279.42.
"The market was very volatile today. Maof options speculators were very active ahead of the expiry date of the May contract on Thursday," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.

Glicksberg said the session opened with a decline of 0.9 percent in the Mishtanim but by midday it had recovered early losses and was up 0.4 percent. Prices came off their peaks towards the end of the day.

"Options speculators used the opportunity created by investors waiting on the sidelines for the interest rate decision and for the Bank Leumi offering on Tuesday," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
The Bank of Israel said after the close of trading that it was holding its key lending rate for June unchanged at an annualised 13.9 percent, the level at which it has been since the end of February.
Glicksberg said a decision to leave the lending rate unchanged would send prices lower on Tuesday.

"Such a decision will be the trigger for a technical correction. The market has been rising for two weeks and it reached an all-time high on Sunday. From a technical point of view a correction would be a natural move," he said.
Bank Leumi, which is making a public offering valued at $150 million on Tuesday, was the most active share falling 2.0 percent to 529 agorot on volume of 11.3 million shekels.

Israel Discount Bank, the third most active, fell 0.75 percent to 368 agorot on volume of 4.5 million shekels. The bank on Monday reported that earnings fell in the first quarter 67 agorot per share from 72 agorot a year earlier.
Clal Industries gained 2.75 percent to 1,806 agorot after it reported first-quarter earnings of 22 agorot, down from 51 agorot a year earlier.
Bank Hapoalim, the second most active issue, closed unchanged at 711 agorot on volume of 4.7 million shekels.
